public_rationale: Marcus predicted a lot of GenAI-driven cybercrime in the coming years. The FBI's 2025 Internet Crime Report, released April 2026, added an AI section for the first time. It counted 22,364 AI-related complaints and nearly $893 million in losses in 2025. Anthropic's August 2025 threat report describes a criminal who used Claude Code to extort at least 17 organizations, and AI-built ransomware sold to other criminals. It concludes that AI has lowered the barriers to sophisticated cybercrime. Read plainly, this is a lot of GenAI-driven cybercrime within the first year after the post. It meets the stated early resolution rule.
limitations: 'A lot' is vague. AI-related complaints were a small share (about 2%) of all IC3 complaints.
The FBI's AI tag relies on victims mentioning AI.
The Anthropic evidence comes from one company's platform.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: There will be a lot of GenAI-driven cybercrime in the coming years.

statement.excerpt: Expect a lot of GenAI-driven cybercrime in the coming years.

our_interpretation: 'In the coming years' sets no fixed deadline. I treat it as an open horizon starting at the post date.

Plain reading of 'a lot': authoritative sources document generative AI being used in cybercrime and fraud on a wide scale, for example tens of thousands of reported crimes or hundreds of millions of dollars in losses in a year, or multiple confirmed large criminal operations.
Cybercrime is read broadly, as authorities use the term, so it includes AI-enabled online fraud and scams.
criteria.support_condition: Law-enforcement or major AI-lab or industry threat reports, published after the post, documenting widespread generative-AI-driven cybercrime in 2025 or 2026.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Authoritative reports after several years showing that generative AI played only a negligible or rare role in cybercrime.

evidence.excerpt: the IC3 report features a section on artificial intelligence, which accounts for 22,364 complaints, costing Americans nearly $893 million.
evidence.explanation: Official US figures for 2025 show more than 22,000 AI-related cybercrime complaints and about $893 million in losses. This meets the large-scale threshold in the early resolution rule.

evidence.excerpt: We recently disrupted a sophisticated cybercriminal that used Claude Code to commit large-scale theft and extortion of personal data. The actor targeted at least 17 distinct organizations
evidence.explanation: An AI developer confirms a large criminal extortion operation run with a generative AI coding agent in 2025. The same report also describes AI-built ransomware sold to other criminals.

evidence.excerpt: AI has lowered the barriers to sophisticated cybercrime. Criminals with few technical skills are using AI to conduct complex operations, such as developing ransomware
evidence.explanation: Anthropic's own finding is that generative AI is widening who can commit sophisticated cybercrime. This fits the forecast of a lot of GenAI-driven cybercrime.

conclusive_event.meets_rule: An official law-enforcement report covering a full year after the post documents tens of thousands of AI-related cybercrime complaints and hundreds of millions of dollars in losses.
